programme.desc: A woman says her ex-husband enables their daughter's addiction.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Three wives send their husbands to Dr. Phil's Man Camp for an attitude adjustment.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: TV Star Nicholas Brendon has been starring in his own private alcohol-fueled drama which has led to multiple arrests and been documented in celebrity magazines, social media and blogs. Nicholas sits down with Dr. Phil -- and abruptly walks offstage. Is Nicholas ready to take the steps needed to save his life and career?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Do you ever feel nervous before posting on social media? Have you ever censored your own thoughts because you worry that you could be criticized or even canceled for posting your beliefs? Dr. Phil and his guests discuss the self-censorship debate on the internet and social media, including the fundamental misunderstanding about the true extent of “freedom of speech” under the First Amendment. Kimberly, a University of Tennessee doctoral candidate, claims her college violated her freedom of speech after a professional conduct committee determined that she had posted unprofessional content to her social media. What rights do colleges have to spy on personal social media posts? Also Tehran Von Ghasri, a comedian who performs on college campuses, says cancel culture gone too far. How does the fear of being canceled affects the jokes he performs for college students or content he posts online? Alexandra, a social media influencer and business owner, says giving opinions about COVID got her censored and three accounts closed. What did she say to get canceled? Dr. Phil also talks with Attorney Robert Shibley, a Senior Fellow at the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE), who says over half of Americans are not saying how they feel for fear of offending others or being canceled. Jessica Levinson, an attorney and a Clinical Professor of Law at Loyola Law School, provides an explanation on the boundaries of the First Amendment. And, Gabrielle Gambrell, a Columbia University and NYU professor, says that social media sites are obligated to monitor hate and dangerous speech. Plus, find out which emojis you are probably using right now are deemed outdated or inappropriate!

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Are deadbeat dads actually dead broke dads? As the American economy struggles, men comprise most of the recent layoffs. In child support cases, are men and women treated equally in the courts, or are the laws out of touch with today's crisis? Dr. Phil's guests, along with Mel Feit, director of the National Center for Men, and Lis Wiehl, author and legal analyst, debate the issue that has many men feeling like the laws are against them.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: He’s a tough-guy afraid of loosing his freedom. She’s been through two ugly divorces. So when the “M” word comes up, they head for the hills. Join these commitment-challenged singles as Dr. Phil uncovers the reasons why they won’t take the plunge. You’ll also meet a man who, after a four years in a loving relationship, doesn’t see the need to get married. To him it’s just a piece of paper. To her it’s a lot more. Find out if it’s really a “deal breaker.”

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Do you have a nosy loved one in your life snooping through your things, questioning your every move and driving you crazy? Dr. Phil has advice.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Is there an adult under your roof, eating your food and taking advantage of you financially? If yes, then you live with a moocher! It's time to stop the enabling and start the accountability.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Craig and Cherie say the last half of their 16-year marriage has been anything but happily-ever-after. Cherie says Craig is chauvinistic, verbally abusive and demands sex, which she admits she only gives him about three to four times a year. Craig says Cherie withholds sex to control him, and as a result, he has become a slave to his anger. Cherie fears the tension in their household is taking a toll on their 11-year-old daughter, who is often caught in the crossfire of their fighting. Dr. Phil challenges the couple to a communication test. Can they heal their wounds and rekindle their romance? Then, meet the couple who inspired the movie, The Vow. Shortly after Kim and Krickitt Carpenter were married, a terrible car crash changed everything. Krickitt lay in a coma for weeks, and awoke with no recognition of her husband. The couple shares their inspiring, though oftentimes heartbreaking, journey of falling in love all over again. How did they find their way back to each other? And what is it like seeing their lives played out on the big screen? If you’ve ever wondered whether love can survive the toughest of challenges, you won’t want to miss this show! This show contains strong sexual content. Viewer discretion advised.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Sixty-four-year-old Josie says she met the love of her life, Victor, on Facebook. Even though he’s Nigerian, 30 years younger, and she’s never physically met him, she insists it’s true love. She’s purchased a ticket to Nigeria and hopes to marry Victor, but her older sister, Carmen, her best friend, Angela, and her 19-year-old son, Anthony, say Josie is acting like a teenage fool. They believe Victor is conning Josie into marrying him for a green card. Dr. Phil took cameras to Nigeria to find Victor to see if he’s telling Josie the truth. Josie’s family says they want Dr. Phil to convince Josie that this relationship will never work. Is Victor who he says he is, and will Josie leave for Nigeria after hearing what Dr. Phil has to say?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Who will Brad choose: his wife or girlfriend?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: They’re self-absorbed, spoiled and entitled brats, otherwise known as Generation Me. MTV correspondent Kim Stolz recently hit the streets of New York to find out how the younger generation feels about this label. Don't miss the candid responses. Then, Bradley, 24, says he wants to be rich and drive a Lamborghini, but he only wants to put in 80 percent of the effort. He still relies on his mom, Christine, to pay his rent and other bills. Will Bradley learn to stand on his own two feet? Plus, Monica says her 18-year-old daughter, Courtney, is an “entitlement princess,” and she gives the teen money just to keep the peace. Will mom and daughter get a wake-up call? And Jean Twenge, author of Generation Me, reveals why many young people are narcissistic.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Dr. Phil continues his conversation with Christina, who emailed him desperate for help for her daughter, Tara, who she says can be an angry monster. Christina left the home when Tara was 13 years old, but now, she says she's worried that her daughter is in a toxic situation with the ex-husband she calls narcissistic and his 22-year-old new wife who is 20 weeks pregnant. Today, meet the new wife and find out if Dr. Phil can help this chaotic triangle.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Dr. Phil's guests haven't even been married a year and are already wondering if it’s time to call it quits.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Contemporary weddings have turned into five-star productions, with couples pulling out all the stops to shine on their special day. But what happens when the bride or groom-to-be starts making diva-like demands? Mike and Jamie agreed to a small Vegas wedding, but that went out the window when Jamie switched her gown three times, rented a limo to drive her one block and upgraded her engagement ring. Mike says that Jamie also made him uninvite all of his friends and cancelled his bachelor party! Are Jamie’s antics a hint of what’s to come in their marriage? Then, Nastassia complains that her husband-to-be, Richard, is cheap. She says he wants her to buy bridal flowers from the grocery store, have her mom sew her gown and even schedule the wedding before year's end so he can get a tax write-off! Will Richard’s tightwad ways force Nastassia to call off the wedding?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Would you rather be right or happy? Dr. Phil talks with some right-fighters who can't settle their debate.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: George and Cindy Anthony speak out for the first time about their daughter, Casey's trial.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: If you think pretty people are immune to heartache, think again. The headlines are filled with stories of striking women who were devastated by infidelity, despite their outward beauty. Dr. Phil sits down with Joey, a husband and father, who says he can’t pass up a pretty face. His wife, Shannon, says he’s slept with close to 100 women since their wedding day. The personal trainer justifies his actions by saying Shannon is overweight and not hot enough for him. Will he get a wake-up call about his cheating ways? Or will his wife take him back yet again? See the shocking text messages to Joey’s mistress, and hear Dr. Phil’s strong message for the hapless husband when a disturbing secret is revealed. Can Dr. Phil encourage Joey to choose another path and look beyond the physical?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Dr. Phil’s guests say they’re not getting any younger, and the race is on to say “I do.” Sharon is 48 and says her biological clock is ticking away. She recently got engaged to a man whom she acknowledges is flawed, and she says her family doesn’t approve of her husband-to-be. Can she get them to accept her beau before they walk down the aisle, or do her relatives have a reason to be concerned? Then, Shea from the reality show Southern Belles: Louisville says that as she was planning her big day, she learned that her fiancé allegedly cheated. Now that the wedding is off, can Shea pick up the pieces and move on? Plus, a dating coach explains the biggest dating mistakes women make.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Do you have someone in your life who's so annoying and frustrating that you just want him or her to go away? What do you do when you're co-parents with someone you can't get along with? And, what if your daughter secretly dated, and then married, a man you despise?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Sue says her husband of 12 years, Andy, is verbally abusive and that she’s so scared of him, she remains submissive -- including getting drunk and having sex with him -- to keep the peace. She says, “If he’s going to kill me, he’s going to kill me. I feel like I’m already dead.” So, why is she worried that Andy will leave her? Andy admits that he can be a bully, loses his temper and calls Sue vile names, but he says the duties of a wife are to have sex, cook and clean -- and Sue doesn't carry her weight around the house. After breaking up numerous times, why do they keep reuniting? And, hear from Sue’s two adult children. What do they say contributes to the chaos in their mom and Andy’s relationship? Is there hope for this couple’s marriage, or should they cut ties?

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: A stay-at-home mother says she can't control her rage, and she takes it out on her kids. Dr. Phil intervenes for the sake of her five precious children.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Some moms don't want to grow up, and others don't want to grow old. Dr. Phil talks to women walking on the wild side and tries to rein them back in!

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: After a Tennessee mother caused an international uproar when she sent her 7-year-old adopted son on a one-way flight back to Russia, the subject of international adoptions is making front-page headlines. Dr. Phil speaks with moms who say they relate to the Tennessee woman, and unless you walk a mile in their shoes, you have no way of understanding. Jane says she had no idea her 2-year-old daughter, Mikhaela, was profoundly deaf and autistic when she adopted her from the Ukraine eight years ago. Jane says the 10-year-old has multiple behavioral disorders and kicks, bites, punches and tries to hurt herself daily, and is getting too strong for her to handle. And, Kristi says all the love in the world couldn’t have helped the baby girl she adopted from China. Kristi says she wasn’t even close to being qualified to parent her now 14-year-old daughter, Tierney, who lives in a behavioral foster home in order to keep Kristi’s other children safe. If you’re thinking of adopting internationally, or if you’re an adoptive parent in crisis, don’t miss today’s show. Learn how to prepare for a cross-cultural adoption, how to get through the adoption process the correct way and what the experts have to say.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: Jessica, a mom of five, sent Dr. Phil a home video so disturbing it brought his wife, Robin, and many audience members to tears. Jessica admits that she’s angry all the time and says she struggles to parent her 7-year-old adopted son, Kristoff. She says she screams at the boy, puts hot sauce in his mouth and places him in a cold shower when he acts up. Attorney and child advocate Areva Martin weighs in. Then, several irate women in the audience give Jessica a piece of their mind.

programme.title: Papelitos
programme.desc: La serie animada “papelitos” cuenta de una manera divertida a los más pequeñitos sobre las simpáticas aventuras de unos animales de papel: Un alce llamado Aristóteles y un pájaro carpintero llamado Tuc-Tuc en el país de papel donde todo por completo está hecho de papel. Divertidas aventuras se acompañan con interesantes clases de manualidades donde los espectadores aprenderán como con papel y cartón crear a todos los personajes de la serie utilizando tijeras y pegamento. El proyecto tiene apoyo de la página web donde están presentados todos los moldes y consejos para crear el mundo de papel. De esta manera el espectador participa en el juego que supone la creación y el desarrollo de muchas habilidades prácticas que distraen a los chicos del encierro permanente de la computadora. El proyecto “Papelitos” es una divertida y didáctica alternativa en lugar de pasar tiempo con la computadora. Toda la acción en el dibujo animado es narrada por una voz en off y repleta de ingeniosos chistes. Cada capítulo dura 5 minutos (la versión sin clase – 4 minutos). La técnica de animación – gráficos 3D que imitan al papel.

programme.title: Glumpers
programme.desc: Si la simple convivencia entre dos personas puede hacer que salten chispas, imagínense lo que podría suceder en una casa habitada por seres con 6 personalidades completamente opuestas. Los Glumpers son una pandilla, un grupo de amigos que viven juntos, las acusadas personalidades de los cuales interactúan continuamente. Si entre los seres humanos una simple discusión en general, va a terminar con sólo un par de insultos, en el caso de los Glumpers puede terminar, en el mejor de los casos, en una explosión atómica.

programme.title: Alex y el Huerto
programme.desc: Cada mañana, la abuela le da una semilla mágica a Alex y él se apresura a la huerta para plantarla. Entonces, va a la fuente a por agua, por lo que puede regar las semillas mágicas. Alex espera con impaciencia para ver como la fruta o vegetal va a crecer. Luego, con destellos de magia, surge de una planta del suelo, y ahí está ... ... un naranjo! Va con una cesta y coge la fruta que van a comer para el almuerzo. Abuela y Alex se sientan a la mesa y comen la fruta o beben su jugo. En Al final, podemos ver y escuchar la explicación de las propiedades básicas de la fruta que acaban de comer.

programme.title: Boom and Reds
programme.desc: Boom & Reds, una serie preescolar. Trata sobre Boom, un cálido y amigable ogro violeta, el cual en cada episodio, intentara averiguar que estan dibujando en el suelo, los reds, una pequeña banda de criaturas de cabezas de champiñones. Desgraciadamente, el echo de que Boom no sea muy inteligente no le ayudará, haciendole pensar en locas sugerencias.

programme.desc: "Faire le tour du monde... sans quitter la Belgique ! C'est la folle aventure dans laquelle nous emmène Nathalie Guirma. Elle fera escale au Tibet, bravera son appréhension de la jungle équatoriale avant de prendre une pause en Papouasie. "

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Matale (Sri Lanka)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine S08
programme.desc: Rencontre avec Denis Lesgourgues, producteur d'armagnac ; avec Isabelle et Patrick Collomb, producteurs de légumes bios. Observation de la migration des oiseaux sur l'étang du Moura avec Nicolas Bernadicou. Visite de la Palmeraie du Sarthou avec Daniel Fort. Détour par Elusa, capitale gallo-romaine.

programme.title: Donner l'gout
programme.desc: Adrian Pastor est le chef péruvien derrière le Projet Yaku, un service de traiteur offert dans la région du Bas-Saint Laurent. Il offre des menus diversifiés où les produits québécois sont apprêtés mêlés aux inspirations péruviennes.

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.desc: Honneur à la cuisine du Sud ! Au menu : artichaut mozzarella et lard valaisan. Également : un bouillon de légumes maison.

programme.title: Ricardo S20
programme.sub-title: Biscuits double chocolat et sables au cafe
programme.desc: Ricardo cuisine des desserts qui manquaient à son répertoire de plus de 7 000 recettes, soit des biscuits double chocolat et des sablés au café. Avec un café-dessert moka pour les accompagner.

programme.title: Les Cueilleurs
programme.desc: Antoine Nicolas se qualifie d'agriculteur du fond des mers. En plein hiver, il n'hésite pas à plonger pour récolter une quinzaine d'espèces d'algues. Débordant de fer, de protéines, de minéraux et de vitamines, elles sont riches en propriétés nutritives mais également en goût.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Douz (Tunisie)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - New Brunswick (Canada)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine S08
programme.desc: Sébastien Lys pêche le mulet à l'oeil et à l'écoute ; Brice Thomas partage sa passion pour la production de sel. Ramassage d'oeufs de raies avec l'association IODDE. Raphaël Musseau, docteur en écologie, et Jean-Claude Barbraud, ornithologue au Muséum national d'histoire naturelle, suivent les cigognes blanches. Visite de Marans.

programme.title: À travers champs S03
programme.sub-title: A travers champs S03 - Cultiver l'IA
programme.desc: "L'intelligence artificielle nous permettra de produire davantage et plus efficacement. Mais il y a avec l'IA certains enjeux importants dont il faut tenir compte, notamment l'accessibilité à la technologie et le partage des données recueillies."

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.desc: La cuisine du Sud est à nouveau à l'honneur ! Au menu : gnocchi aux blettes et rösti d'Ardèche.

programme.title: Ricardo S20
programme.desc: Ricardo utilise les aliments oubliés au congélateur pour préparer un hamburger steak aux champignons, une purée de pommes de terre au maïs et au beurre d'harissa, en guise d'accompagnement, suivie d'un lait frappé aux petits fruits pour dessert.

programme.title: Les Cueilleurs
programme.desc: Le thé du labrador est la plante préférée de Mélanie Sheehy. Après un détour en Colombie-Britannique, où elle apprend le pouvoir des plantes, l'herboriste cueille aujourd'hui cet or vert dans sa région, le Lac-St-Jean. Préoccupée par la pérennité de sa ressource, elle ne récolte qu'une partie des feuilles du plant.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Dieppe (New Brunswick, Canada)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: La Recette de Guy Martin S08
programme.sub-title: Quenelles de brochets au coulis d'ecrevisses
programme.desc: Le chef étoilé Guy Martin présente les produits emblématiques du terroir français et propose une recette pour les accommoder.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine S08
programme.desc: "Hugo Guinet, maraîcher bio et éleveur de poules, vend ses produits directement au consommateur. Tout savoir sur le cavage des truffes avec le trufficulteur Philippe de Santis, qui propose les précieux tubercules au marché d'Aups. La végétation du massif des Maures et la biodiversité sous-marine de la lagune du Brusc."

programme.title: À travers champs S03
programme.sub-title: A travers champs S03 - A vos risques et perils
programme.desc: "L'agriculture est un domaine où les impondérables sont nombreux. Des plans d'assurance spécifiques existent et des outils ont été mis en place pour venir en aide aux producteurs agricoles en cas de coup dur. Sont-ils suffisants ?"

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.desc: Honneur à la cuisine italienne. Au menu : pasta e fagioli, des pâtes aux haricots.

programme.title: Ricardo S20
programme.desc: Réconfort sucré pour la fin de semaine : un popcorn au caramel, lime et noix de coco, du fudge maison et des éclats de tire-éponge enrobés de chocolat.

programme.title: Les Cueilleurs
programme.desc: La cueillette de l'oursin peut s'avérer difficile. Joseph Roy et Anthony Jean, deux plongeurs professionnels, pratiquent ce métier plus que particulier à Cacouna, dans le bas du Fleuve.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Sierra Vista (Arizona, USA)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Dublin (Irlande)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine
programme.desc: Aux portes du Verdon, Hugo Guinet récolte des épinards bio et élève des poules. Philippe de Santis part à la recherche de truffes. Une fois nettoyée, sa précieuse cueillette est vendue sur le marché d'Aups. Pour finir, partez en randonnée en montagne à la découverte de la biodiversité.

programme.title: À travers champs S03
programme.sub-title: A travers champs S03 - Beaucoup a apprendre
programme.desc: "Travailler en agriculture demande une expertise certaine et ce, dans plusieurs domaines. Heureusement, tant pour préparer la relève agricole qu'au chapitre de la formation continue, il y a au Québec une offre académique vaste et diversifiée."

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.desc: Au menu : oeufs pochés à l'oseille et flan au caramel.

programme.title: LA CUISINE D’ISABELLE ET RICARDO
programme.desc: Isabelle cuisine un poulet à la sauce crémeuse aux piments poblano alors que Ricardo nous présente les différents piments et poivrons.

programme.title: Les Cueilleurs
programme.desc: Entre distillateur et aventurier, Baptiste Gissinger cueille tous les aromates qui composent ses gins. Avec des herbes locales de vingt-cinq pays différents, chaque création est unique. Le cueilleur de genévrier aime dire qu'il met un terroir dans une bouteille.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Loches (France)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Aups (Haut Var, France)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine
programme.desc: Direction l'Île d'Oléron, où Benoit Simon, maraîcher, raconte la relance d'un oignon de la région, délaissé il y a plus de 50 ans. Nicholas Wherkhoven présente sa production d'huîtres Marennes Oléron dont les fameuses claires. L'association I.O.D.D.E. redonne vie à des déchets naturels.

programme.title: À travers champs S03
programme.sub-title: A travers champs S03 - L'evolution des mentalites
programme.desc: "Alors que l'agriculture a longtemps été vue favorablement par la grande majorité de la population, l'évolution des mentalités, surtout en ce qui concerne le bien-être animal, a changé la perception des façons de faire."

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.desc: Le poisson est à l'honneur, et plus particulièrement la perche. Au menu : tortellini à la perche.

programme.title: LA CUISINE D’ISABELLE ET RICARDO
programme.sub-title: Tarte aux tomates et salade de courgettes
programme.desc: Isabelle s'inspire du potager avec deux recettes qui mettent à l'honneur les légumes frais : une tarte aux tomates et une salade de courgettes au basilic.

programme.title: Les Cueilleurs
programme.desc: À Rivière-Saint-Jean, Alex Beaudin et Alexis Parisée préparent leur motoneige pour une expédition en forêt. Sur la Côte-Nord, par une température de -17, les deux amis d'enfance vont ramasser le poivre des dunes. Cette épice particulière s'utilise aussi bien avec les viandes que dans du gin ou de la bière.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.desc: Every episode offers a different journey! Xavier Petit, cameraman reporter, invites us to explore a country, a town, a people and, of course, a traditional market and a local speciality.

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.desc: Every episode offers a different journey! Xavier Petit, cameraman reporter, invites us to explore a country, a town, a people and, of course, a traditional market and a local speciality.

programme.desc: Le chef étoilé Guy Martin présente les produits emblématiques du terroir français et propose une recette pour les accommoder.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine
programme.desc: Dans les collines bisontines, Isabelle Cerisier fait visiter son maraîchage à l'ancienne, où les moutons déambulent au milieu des cultures. Caroline et Romain ouvrent les portes de leur ferme où ils pratiquent élevage et vente de laitages. Découvrez enfin, les terrasses en pierres sèches et le marais de Saône.

programme.title: À travers champs S03
programme.sub-title: A travers champs S03 - L'esprit de communaute
programme.desc: "L'esprit de communauté a toujours été important en agriculture. Il est encore bien vivant aujourd'hui, notamment chez la nouvelle génération qui privilégie un modèle d'agriculture où l'on mise davantage sur la coopération que la compétition."

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.desc: Annick et Simon nous préparent un quinoa à la vinaigrette de fèves. En dessert, une crème brûlée.

programme.title: LA CUISINE D’ISABELLE ET RICARDO
programme.desc: Dans cet épisode 100 % chocolaté, Isabelle prépare des biscuits au chocolat ainsi que des sucettes glacées au chocolat, parfaits pour les becs sucrés.

programme.title: Les Cueilleurs
programme.desc: Antoine Nicolas se qualifie d'agriculteur du fond des mers. En plein hiver, il n'hésite pas à plonger pour récolter une quinzaine d'espèces d'algues. Débordant de fer, de protéines, de minéraux et de vitamines, elles sont riches en propriétés nutritives mais également en goût.

programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine
programme.desc: Dans le Bas-Vivarais, Christophe Chaussy ouvre les portes d'une ferme familiale entre élevage de porcs et fabrication de charcuterie. Des vignes au chai, Myriam Oddon détaille les étapes de la fabrication du vinaigre. Pour finir, le voile est levé sur des secrets cachés dans certaines roches montagneuses.

programme.title: À travers champs S03
programme.sub-title: A travers champs S03 - Les changements climatiques
programme.desc: "Marie-Claude Lortie rencontre des spécialistes du climat pour connaître les impacts du changement climatique au Québec, ainsi que des agriculteurs qui s'adaptent aux nouvelles conditions dans lesquelles pratiquer leur métier."

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S07
programme.sub-title: Barbecue et salade de lentilles au citron vert
programme.desc: Annick a quitté sa cuisine pour celle du chalet ! Au menu : filet mignon de cochon au barbecue et salade de lentilles.

programme.title: LA CUISINE D’ISABELLE ET RICARDO
programme.desc: Isabelle et Ricardo cuisinent deux recettes qui se font en grande quantité : du boeuf braisé à la coréenne et des sandwichs au boeuf braisé à la coréenne.

programme.title: C’est plus qu’un jardin S03
programme.desc: "Véronique Claveau et Bryan Audet se lancent dans l'aventure potagère sous les conseils d'Édith et Dany. Ces derniers découvrent aussi l'emplacement du futur jardin pédagogique de l'Académie des Sacrés-Coeurs de Saint-Bruno."

programme.title: Pays et marchés du monde
programme.sub-title: Pays et marches du monde - Amboseli (Kenya)
programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine
programme.sub-title: L'enclave des Papes et le pays de Grignan
programme.desc: Dans l'enclave des Papes et le pays de Grignan, Christian Mérin part au pied de ses chênes truffiers dénicher le précieux champignon. Justine Vigne présente son travail de vigneronne en biodynamie. Suivez ensuite des bénévoles en plein ramassage de déchets avant de découvrir des mystères contenus dans la roche.

programme.title: Les quatre coins de l’assiette S02
programme.desc: "Le chef Domenico Giammarella prépare un semifreddo au miel de sarrasin avec compote de framboises et rhubarbe, meringue de framboises et biscuit Linzer au miel et à la rhubarbe."

programme.title: PIQUE ASSIETTE S08
programme.desc: Premières recettes de la saison mitonnées par Annick Jeanmairet et Simon Romang : des poireaux vinaigrette au jaune d'oeuf confit. En dessert : une mousse au chocolat à la fève tonka. Découverte du jour : des cacahuètes 100 % suisses.

programme.title: LA CUISINE D’ISABELLE ET RICARDO
programme.sub-title: Tarte au citron et au pavot
programme.desc: Isabelle, en compagnie de Ricardo, prépare une tarte au citron et au pavot meringuée. Elle nous montre aussi comment réaliser une cuisson à blanc avec des pois de cuisson.

programme.title: C’est plus qu’un jardin S03
programme.desc: "La famille Claveau-Audet construit une couche froide et revalorise ses hémérocalles en les offrant aux voisins. La brigade de l'Académie des Sacrés-Coeurs fait du vermicompostage, détourbe le potager et Édith découvre son projet d'hydroponie."

programme.desc: À chaque épisode, un voyage ! Xavier Petit, caméraman reporter, nous fait découvrir un pays, une ville, un peuple et, bien sûr, un marché traditionnel et une spécialité locale.

programme.desc: Le chef étoilé Guy Martin présente les produits emblématiques du terroir français et propose une recette pour les accommoder.

programme.title: Epicerie Fine S08
programme.desc: Dans le Larzac, à Nant, Marion Renoud-Lias et Romain Debord cultivent des plantes et des fleurs, tout en testant des recettes de gin. Émilie et Alexandre Vialettes élèvent des brebis de race Lacaune et produisent du bleu fermier. Découvrir les eaux précieuses des Causses et les mythes enchanteurs des Canalettes.

programme.title: La vigne en heritage
programme.desc: Quand les grands domaines viticoles français maintiennent la tradition d'un travail en famille...

programme.title: La vigne en heritage

programme.title: Pique-Assiette
programme.desc: Le poisson est à l'honneur avec le chef Pierre Crepaud ! Au menu : ceviche de perche, un plat d'inspiration péruvienne, puis perche pané avec une chapelure ultra croustillante !

programme.title: Ricardo S20
programme.desc: Afin d'utiliser les restes de citrouille d'Halloween, Ricardo propose deux recettes pour en cuisiner la chair et les graines : un cari de citrouille et de poulet et un pesto de graines de citrouille.

programme.title: Amuse-gueule
programme.desc: Au menu : omble chevalier en papillote avec le chef Jean-Marc Soldati, l'alimentation des seniors avec la diététicienne Florence Authier, fêtes et gastronomie à travers le monde, idée dessert avec Amandine Freudiger.

programme.title: La Recette de Guy Martin S08
programme.sub-title: Costeleta de vitela, espelta e chantarelles salteadas
programme.desc: O chef estrelado pelo Guia Michelin, Guy Martin, apresenta produtos emblemáticos da França e sugere uma receita para prepará-los.

programme.title: Safran & saveurs by chef Simo
programme.sub-title: Yassa poulet senegalais et zaalouk parfume marocain
programme.desc: Chef Simo crée une alliance entre Sénégal et Maroc avec un yassa poulet accompagné d'un zaalouk parfumé, le tout rehaussé par une sauce Paris-Dakar. Un régal panafricain !

programme.title: Epicerie Fine S08
programme.desc: "Direction la ferme des Jovents, où Camille et Rudy Michel proposent d'étonnantes glaces au lait de chèvre. Près de Tourves, Isé Crébely et Bruno Cayron produisent des légumes anciens et oubliés en maraîchage biologique. Découverte : de jour ou de nuit, les petites habitudes des scorpions et insectes."

programme.title: Donner l'gout
programme.desc: On rencontre Mohamed, le chef propriétaire du Marin d'eau douce, à Carleton-sur-Mer. Avec sa femme, Iman, et leurs trois filles, il tient un restaurant où on peut retrouver les saveurs de son Maroc natal combiné à des produits québécois.

programme.title: Pique-Assiette
programme.desc: Honneur à la cuisine italienne avec la cheffe Francesca Fucci. Elle nous présente sa recette de pâtes à base de parmesan, d'oeufs et de... pain sec. Réduit en chapelure, ce pain remplace la farine.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: After three classical Strongman events – Dead lift, Loading and Front hold – and one historical, Chopper Pull for the first time in history of Strongman, now we go to find out who will take title in Romania. This is the second stage in Romania and it remains to be seen who will win the title; Aivars, Travis or Krzyzstof?

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: The next destination of Strongman Champions League is in a piece of paradise on earth – Curacao. We bring to you some special Strongman events like the Rock Lift, Tug of War and Weight for Height in this episode.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: We're in Zrenjanin, Serbia, again a fantastic stage in the SCL WORLD SERIES TOUR 2024, five events including a super human Yoke race. Who will be the yellow leader for the coming season and take the title with 25 championship points?

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: This is the last competition before the grand finals. After the first three events Zageris is in top place, but can O’Hagan, Baggott, Petursson and Ortmayer step into the final? Last chance some of them will find through events like Forward Hold, Truck Pull, Dead Lift and loading very big objects.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.sub-title: SCL 2018 Season 5, Episode 14, Road to Mexico
programme.desc: We bring you 50 minutes of Strongman inside. Fears, inspiration, courage, the best and worst from our finalists and their expectation of the finals. We also go to Poland and Germany to represent one day in the training of Krzysztof Radzikowski and Dennis Kohlruss. See all the finalists for Mexico in their comfort zone here, with their backgrounds /motivations /family and friends.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.sub-title: SCL 2018 Season 5, Episode 15, Mexico - World Finals (Part 1)
programme.desc: The first part of the Strongman Champions League 2018 finals in Mexico. The last twelve athletes all pushing their boundaries and testing their limits to take the World title.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.sub-title: SCL 2018 Season 5, Episode 16, Mexico - World Finals (Part 2)
programme.desc: After 11 months and 14 competitions all over the world, it all comes down to the final in this episode. The strongmen must show their best skills and every mistake is expensive, so their concentration must be at the highest possible level. Will Krzysztof manage to take off back or will Dainis maintain his lead?

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.sub-title: SCL 2019 Season 6, Episode 1, World Strongest Viking
programme.desc: This year 14 athletes from all over the world came to Fefor to compete in 6 cruel events. We'll see typical Viking disciplines on very heavy conditions in land of snow and ice, World records and athletes like the title defender Krzysztof Radzikowski, strongest guys from Holland and Germany and many more

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: The next stop in strongest league of the world is muscle capital, largest number of strong shoulders per capita in the World and of course, the most powerful host in Strongman champions league on the planet. It’s a FIBO - the biggest expo on planet Earth and the second stage of 2019 Strongman champions league, in Cologne, Germany.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: On a spectacular beach in Alanya, the MLO Strongman Champions League Turkey was viewed by thousands of spectators over a two day battle. With 12 athletes at the start over 6 cruel events, like Marble Stone Lift, Truckpull and Deadlift cars. And with the comeback of Travis Ortmayer / USA, former stone king and world ranked competitor. Winner of several SCL stages in the past.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: Four times Strongest Man of Holland, Alex Moonen and the “Flying Dutchman” Kelvin de Ruiter competing here in Holland against 12 other strongest men in the world. There were 6 events in total, and 3 in this episode: The first event, a truckpull of 17.000 kg over 25 meters in max 75 seconds, was a real hard pull Also for the World Champion Truckpull, Holland’s runner-up Kelvin de Ruiter, but watch his amazing technique here.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: Strongest Man of Holland, Alex Moonen and the “Flying Dutchman” Kelvin de Ruiter, competing in Holland against 12 other strongest men in the world. There were 6 events in total, 3 in this second episode; a Viking-press of 150 kg with the current world record holder Luke Herrick. The fifth event, a front hold of 25 kg is loved or hated by the athletes and lastly, the Stones of Strength.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: An unbelievable TANK PULL of 50.000 kg was at the stage of SCL RUSSIA. Never seen this before! Not only a tank pull was done here but also the Viking Press/ Deadlift Max and Log lift reps were spectacular events to see here in Russia. With Mikhail Koklyaev also as event presenter, the former top 3 world strongest man from Russia was there

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: In this year’s edition on The Balkan Peninsula, we have competing the new talent from Estonia Marko Remlik together with Sebastian Kurek from Poland and yellow leader Kelvin de Ruiter

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: Mateusz Kieliszkowski from Poland and Aivars Smaukstelis from Latvia are the strongman future of these days. Mateusz is the best man in the World at the moment to defeat. Only 25 years and such a fantastic strongman. They come here only for a win. But there are 12 more Strong athletes in this episode who want the title of Finland as well.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: Mateusz Is leading after day 1 (previous episode) with close behind him Aivars Smaukstelis and Zake Muluzi from the UK. All very exciting! 5 events in this episode: Log Lift, Fram Walk, Deadlift, Sack Throw (Weight for Height), Loading medley.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: In this stage we have a new strong debutant: Oleg Sylka from the Ukraine. He is the new talent, who will stand up against the old champions like ZSydrunas Savickas and Brian Shaw and the Stoltman Brother from the UK. This new talent Oleg is a great character and we will see him flame in the episode in Portugal.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: In Callio is the deepest mine of Europe/ 1500 meter deep, whereas the MLO Strongman Champions League also did 1 event. The Forward Hold, on a 1500 dept/ also a kind of new record/ as it was never done before. Spectacular and new in Strongman sport.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: Kelvin de Ruiter is here to defend his SCL World Truck Pull Championships title. But this year, another strong field wants his title. Over 3 different pulls with 3 different trucks, and 14 athletes at the start, it will be difficult for everybody.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: SCL edition Curacao 2019 was a great event, twelve power boys from all over made a great show at the white beaches, and 35 degrees Celsius heat in the Carrabean Islands. Two events were held on Friday at the beach of beautiful resort Sunscape, the other three were held near the world famous floating bridge at Willemstad on Saturday night.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: Hosted at Meydan Grandstand in Dubai, the Strongman Champions League had some really big names in the list like Mateusz Kieliszkowski from Poland, Brian Shaw from the USA and Krzysztof Radzikowski. In front of the Burj Khalifa the athletes do the deadlift max and 4 other heavy events at another spot in Dubai.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: With new places on the calendar, over 16 stages, broadcasting in over 100 countries and in its 13th year, the MLO Strongman Champions League (SCL) can be seen truly as the biggest strongman league in the world. The last stage over 2 episodes of the MLO Strongman Champions League, were held in Porto, Portugal. This competition in Portugal is full of memorable performances and strong results.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: With new places on the calendar, over 16 stages, broadcasting in over 100 countries and in its 13th year, the MLO Strongman Champions League (SCL) can be seen truly as the biggest strongman league in the world. This competition in Portugal is full of memorable performances and strong results and this is the final!

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: The spectacular Fefor Arena hosted for the 8th time the Worlds Strongest Viking, part of the SCL World Series. But with the absence of former title holders its anyones game. Again, a very spectacular episode of the Strongman Champions League here in Norway.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League
programme.desc: In this episode, the Titan, former double World champion from Latvia will compete against his fellow countryman and the current World champion - Aivars Smaukstelis. With 8 events over 2 stages the contestants are pushed to their limits in Finland.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2023
programme.sub-title: US Open 2023 – Women’s Senior Pro Doubles Semifinal – Bagby & Bellamy vs Dawson & Williams
programme.desc: Catch all the action from the Women's Senior Pro Doubles Semifinal 1 at the 2023 US Open Pickleball Championships held in Naples, Florida. This semifinal match features top senior pros Nathalie Bagby and Beth Bellamy facing Jennifer Dawson and Bonnie Williams in a high-stakes contest. Expert commentary highlights key strategies, player strengths, and match dynamics including powerful serves from Ava Welsher, tactical lobs, and intense court positioning. Follow how the players adjust to crowd pressure and timeouts in this best-of-three game format. Get ready for a thrilling showdown in one of pickleball’s premier senior pro events.

programme.title: World Pickleball League (WPBL)
programme.sub-title: WPBL 2026 - Bengaluru vs Delhi - Day 4 Tie 2
programme.desc: The World Pickleball League Season 2 returns to the Jio World Garden in Mumbai for an electrifying Tie 8 showdown. The defending champions, Bengaluru Jawans—led by coach Oliver Strecker and backed by owners Atlee and Priya—return to the court for the first time since their dominant opening night performance. They face a determined Delhi Dilwale squad, coached by Wesley Gabrielsson, who are looking to climb the standings after a hard-fought tie-break victory in their previous outing.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2025
programme.sub-title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2025 – Pro Women’s Doubles – Waters & Waters vs Schull & Cavataio
programme.desc: Filmed at the US Open Pickleball Championships in Naples, Florida, this Pro Women’s Doubles matchup features the powerhouse mother-daughter team Leigh and Anna Leigh Waters, known for their aggressive tactics and flawless communication. They square off against promising challengers Alexa Schull and Ava Cavataio, who bring fearless shot-making and tight teamwork to the court. From baseline drives to net duels, this clash of generations delivers fast-paced action, strategic rallies, and plenty of highlight-worthy moments.

programme.title: National Collegiate Pickleball Association (NCPA)
programme.sub-title: NCPA Utah Regional 2025 - Team Match 1 - Utah Tech vs. Utah State
programme.desc: Welcome to Championship Sunday at the NCPA Utah Regional 2025. This Round of 16 Collegiate Team Match pits the 5th-seeded Utah Tech against the 12th-seeded, but formidable, Utah State squad. The action takes place at Club Pickleball USA in Orem, Utah. Both teams are competing for a coveted bid to the National Championship in Saint Louis, Missouri, which features a $30,000 prize pool.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Kyoya Fujitia
programme.desc: In the Marathon Peak Performance for the 8th stop of the 2023 Bassmaster Elite Series season, watch Kyoya Fujita take the title at Lake Champlain for the first B.A.S.S. win of his career. The young Japanese prodigy stormed to 5 Top 10's in his Rookie season.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Lee Livesay
programme.desc: Walk on the wild side with Lee Livesay and his entire week at Lake Fork as he looked to go back to back on his home lake. Livesay was the local favorite with the most amount of knowledge at Lake Fork, but sometimes that can bite you. In the Marathon Peak Performance of the Event, Livesay wins his third Elite Series title and fourth overall Bassmaster victory in just a span of 18 months.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie led three days of the Elite Series event at the Sabine River and rode a great two days of fishing to the winners circle in his return year to the Bassmaster Elites. He is the Marathon Peak Performance at the Sabine.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Joey Cifuentes
programme.desc: First year Bassmaster Elite Series pro Joey Cifuentes dominated the Lake Seminole Elite event and took his first pro-level victory. Cifuentes outlasted the field with a four-day total of 85 pounds, 2 ounces. In this Marathon Peak Performance you can watch his winning week.

programme.title: Peak Performance -Patrick Walters
programme.desc: Through just 5 years on the Bassmaster Elite Series, Patrick Walters has an incredible resume. He added another accolade with a win at Lake Murray, doing so in impressive fashion. Congratulations to ‪@patrickwaltersfishing5121‬, he is the Marathon Peak Performance at the 5th stop of the 2024 season.

programme.title: Peak Performance - John Garrett
programme.desc: The Marathon Peak Performance for the third stop of the Elite Series season features John Garrett and his impressive week at the Harris Chain of Lakes. The former College Champion and current Elite Series rookie led wire to wire and got his first blue trophy in just his 3rd event of the season.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Will Davis Jr.
programme.desc: In his Marathon Peak Performance of the week, watch Will Davis Jr. win his first Bassmaster Elite Series title in dramatic fashion on his home body of water. Davis won by just 2 ounces over Brandon Palaniuk, making it the closest margin of victory since Toledo Bend of 2011.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Brock Mosley
programme.desc: In his 8-year Bassmaster Elite Series career, Brock Mosley has been so close to major titles but fallen just short with 5 2nd place finishes and even more Top 10’s. Watch Mosley put four great days together on his way to his first Elite Series title at the 2023 Folds of Honor Bassmaster Elite at the Sabine River and take home the Marathon Peak Performance!

programme.title: Peak Performance - Justin Hammer
programme.desc: ‪@justinhamnerfishing‬ followed his passion and that dream led him to the Bassmaster Elite Series. After a few years on the Elites, he was in the catbird seat of the 2024 Bassmaster Classic where his lifelong dream came true and he became the World Champion of bass fishing. Watch his week unfold at Grand Lake O' the Cherokees in Oklahoma.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Trey Mckinney
programme.desc: One week after turning 19 years old, Trey McKinney became the youngest Bassmaster Elite Series Champion after landing 130 pounds, 15 ounces at Lake Fork for the 2nd stop of the season. Watch his week unfold in this Marathon Peak Performance feature.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Joey Cifuentes
programme.desc: In the Marathon Peak Performance at the 7th stop of the 2023 Bassmaster Elite Series season, Joey Cifuentes takes the title at Lake St. Clair by going against the grain. Cowboy Cifuentes is a Rookie on the Elite Series but with two wins in 2023, he has wowed the fishing world.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Brandon Lester
programme.desc: ‪@BrandonLesterFishing‬ fished a flawless week at Pickwick Lake for the 6th stop of the 2022 Bassmaster Elite Series season. Lester took the title and won his first Elite Series title and his second B.A.S.S. win this year. Congratulations to Lester, the Marathon Peak Performance at Pickwick.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Bryant Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt is one of the winningest anglers in professional fishing and his great track record is noted on grassy river fisheries. Schmitt ended 2022 with a big victory on the Mighty Mississippi River in La Crosse, Wisconsin. Watch his stellar week in the Marathon Peak Performance of the tournament.

programme.title: Peak Performance - John Crews
programme.desc: The Marathon Peak Performance at the St. Johns River went to ‪@JohnCrews‬ as he led wire to wire to win his second career Bassmaster Elite Series event. Watch his week from behind the lens as he strived for another major tournament victory as a professional fisherman.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cliff Prince
programme.desc: Cliff Prince dials us in on his 1/2 ounce Chatterbait setup that helped him win the Bassmaster Elite at Wheeler Lake. He also dishes the details on his magic spot and why he thinks the morning was incredible every day for him.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Seth Feider
programme.desc: Seth Feider goes through his wood jig and grass jig setup. He explains the differences in line tie and weed guard why he likes a short hook and his colors for flipping. Whether it's docks laydowns shoreline grass or submerged vegetation; Feider will often rely on a jig to get it done. His favorite size is a 5/8 ounce.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin sets up the calendar for Florida's Spawn Cycle. Depending on weather spawn can start in south Florida as early as Thanksgiving week and extend through May of the next year. Martin gives his take on the difference of a lake like Okeechobee and the St. Johns River farther north.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tucker Smith
programme.desc: Tucker Smith talks about finding hard spots on Lake Fork with his side imaging throughout practice and then using his forward facing sonar to execute and catch fish throughout the tournament. He utilized a 7-inch minnow on spinning tackle with varying head sizes as well as a 3/4-ounce football jig on the final day.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Arey
programme.desc: Matt Arey talks about the importance of varying your retrieve with swimbaits over structure like brush piles. This is something that can be done with or without forward facing sonar as Arey describes the trial and error used prior to newer technology.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Lester
programme.desc: Brandon Lester gives us two key factors he relies on when choosing between a Jig and Texas Rig which is often a debate in the Fall fishing season. Profile and rate of fall depending on the seasonal conditions are considerations for the two-time BASS winner.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Emil Wagner
programme.desc: Emil Wagner sheds light on his favorite bait for winter fishing especially on spotted bass lakes like Lanier. With jig head minnows neko rigs and dropshots becoming popular everyone forgot about the shaky head.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock relies on burning a crankbait over grass rock and stumps during late winter and pre-spawn. He ups his line size to keep the bait higher and uses a 7'4" rod for longer casts and ripping it free from grass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Bernie Schultz gives his three trusted lures when he is covering water to develop a pattern in the spring. He balances a spinnerbait swim jig and chatterbait when he approaches different types of cover.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock talks about one of the most fun techniques and lures that is so effective in the Fall season. Covering water with a Berkley Choppo is essential and allows Shryock to burn through dead water in no time with this approach and it is a tournament winning formula.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston goes over his two main lures for bed fishing at the St. Johns River en route to his first Elite Series victory. Johnston also explains his use of Perspective Mode when seeing bed fish in low visibility times.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Alex Wetherell
programme.desc: Alex Wetherell discusses two soft plastics he uses around his home in Connecticut and down south when the calendar hits December. Balls of bait equal bass for Wetherell as they actively feed even when the water temperatures are cooler at the end of the year. Bass aren’t nearly as lethargic as we once believed years ago.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson pulls out his favorite bait for the fall when the water temperatures are falling and in many situations the water level is falling too. When the bass start keying in on crawfish with cooling water J-Will knows its jig season. With living rubber skirted jigs Williamson fishes a 1/2 ounce or 3/4 ounce jig and never goes lighter than 1/2 ounce. He will also target brush early and as it continues to cool down will move to rock through the winter.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes tackles where the fish go when they finish spawning but the water temperatures aren't at their hottest yet like they will be later in the summer. Cifuentes dives into three different baits that are useful around lakes with standing timber for the last week of May as we head into June.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Latuso
programme.desc: Logan Latuso discusses a big key in the summer months...SHADE. This underrated aspect of the summer can get you some of the biggest bites of your day and it seemingly gets better as the day progresses. Take notes from Latuso and don't run your shade pattern too early to ensure some of your best success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew relies on a jerkbait from late fall through the spawn whether using electronics or not. He keeps two color options: translucent for sunny or clear water and solid for cloudy or stained conditions.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses fishing a jerkbait around Christmas time and how two of his baits act totally different. Christie breaks down how the Smithwick Rogue and Booyah Flash Point react different on the same cadence. Water temperatures in the 40's Christie opts for the Rogue. Meanwhile he sees positive results with the quick-working Flash Point with temperatures in the 50's and even 60's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: Brandon Palaniuk shares the three baits he used to win the Bassmaster Elite Series at Lake Okeechobee: a Megabass Kanata jerkbait and two Megabass crankbaits (Big M and a prototype). Fishing one spot aggressively led to some of the biggest strikes seen on Bassmaster LIVE.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Cobb
programme.desc: Brandon Cobb gives his top picks for effective baits on lakes with blueback herring. Spotted bass and largemouth will get hyper focused on blueback herring when they exist on a body of water and Cobb knows these baits will work throughout the year and not a certain specific season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher gives his take on a few productive lures in the prespawn and how he balances their uses to be most effective while on the water. Should you use a Chatterbait where a jig could also work or vice versa he attacks this and more in this scenario.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt highlights how different SPRO Aruku Shad versions and hook sizes enhance performance based on season cover and action. He adjusts for fall rates with yo-yo or straight retrieves and downsizes when the bite is tough.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tyler Williams
programme.desc: Tyler Williams reveals the details to his 3/4 ounce jig he uses across the country. Upsizing his line can help slow the fall of his heavy jig along with pairing the jig with a big bulky trailer. Williams will use this jig around docks brush piles ledges and when targeting specific fish on his forward-facing sonar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Hamner
programme.desc: Justin Hamner gives his strategy to catch key bass each day of competition and how he utilized multiple kinds of jerkbaits and mixed in a jig to catch the majority of his weight on Grand Lake in the 2024 Bassmaster Classic.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jake Whitaker
programme.desc: Jake Whitaker talks about the shallow bite windows that open up even with 100 degree days in the south. Whitaker leans on a topwater toad around any sort of cover that could hold fish. Anglers may get less bites in the heat of the summer but they can be the quality you need in a tournament.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Cox
programme.desc: John Cox gives a look at two of his favorite topwater lures and ones he trusts in the Fall. Whether it's around grass wood or rock both of these lures are on his front deck this time of year. Cox experimented with a longer frog rod this season and it helped him land a 3rd place finish at Wheeler Lake.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin gives us his version of Thanksgiving turkey and fixings with this three-bait lineup this time of year. He has a bait for every level of the water column depending on how the fish are acting and where you're fishing this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Garrett
programme.desc: John Garrett runs down the three baits that were key for his win on the Harris Chain of Lakes. Garrett rotated between these techniques depending on how the fish were positioned and their aggressiveness on the shell bar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen explains his two-pronged approach at the St. Johns River sticking to one area for four days using a black and blue swim jig and a flipping jig. He highlights his swim jig cadence and the importance of his flipping jig falling into hard cover

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson provides a solution to those tricky bass that are days from spawning and sit high in the water column. Not only does a jig provide great opportunities for good catches but a swimbait also entices those big females to commit.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube walks us through one of his favorite techniques in tournaments and fun fishing. Dube gives his take on practicing with a Glide Bait and his strategy to convert followers into fish that will commit to biting.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher breaks down his single bait that produced a record winning margin and over 118 pounds of bass at the Pasquotank River. Flipping a Rapala CrushCity Bronco Bug to shallow roamers and spawning bass was his strategy. He utilized his forward facing sonar to pick out fish among the cover littered on the bottom.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Trey McKinney
programme.desc: Lake Fork Champion Trey McKinney gives his lure arsenal as he adjusted daily to the changing fish for the second stop of the Elite Series season. Early in the event he used a jerkbait and jig head minnow combo but as the weather warm and conditions changed his baits adapted. Culminating on the final day were multiple baits contributed to his 130-15 tournament weight.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt pulls 4 swim jigs out of his tackle box to showcase their effectiveness on different pieces of cover and depths. A simple trailer change can help Schmitt's swim jig stay shallow or go deeper. Schmitt gives the nuts and bolts to swim jig fishing his way and style.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Clifford Pirch
programme.desc: Clifford Pirch gives us a few ways to rig a drop shot if you're specifically targeting smallmouth and spotted bass. Threading his worm on weedless is his ideal setup but when fishing for smallmouth and spotted bass they tend to be more open water and less obstructions around. That's when Pirch will opt for a few other methods for fall rate and action.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Paul Marks
programme.desc: Paul Marks shows off his single bait that produced in two different situations depending on how he rigged it. The Zoom Fluke Stick in Natural Shad contributed almost all of his weight in his Elite victory at Lake Hartwell. His first approach was rigging it weightless to throw on shallow points where bass pushed blueback herring to feed in the morning then he switch to a shakey head in the afternoons.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Parks
programme.desc: Logan Parks discusses a strategy he employed at Wheeler during his first Top 10. Varying line size can help crankbaits run different depth and retrieved faster or slower. It's something he recommends during the summer months when schools are forming offshore or have been fished for frequently.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Herren
programme.desc: Matt Herren goes through the process of fishing current seams on rivers with a spinnerbait. No matter time of year water current is a great place to find fish and target where bass are positioned and if you find the correct lineup it can be fast action. Herren recommends a 1/2-ounce to 3/4-ounce compact spinnerbait to avoid snags and hangups and control the bait despite the current pushing and washing the spinnerbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Patrick
programme.desc: Kyle Patrick gives his approach for fishing for less pressured fish during the spawning months of the year. The fishing myth around the spawn is that bass have to go to the bank to do their yearly spawn when in reality fish can spawn much deeper and will take longer to do so.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew talks about one of his favorite fun-fishing lures which is the Umbrella Rig aka Alabama Rig. LeHew utilizes this in multiple ways as he can cover water around shallow cover like he would with a spinnerbait but also with his electronics around deeper offshore structure.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Todd Auten
programme.desc: Todd Auten goes over three Chatterbait variations that have made the South Carolina pro successful with this technique. Whether it's color selection trailer options or getting the bait to ride high in the water column or fall fast Auten has his process. 1. White/CChartuese w/Zoom Shimmer Shad 2. Black/Blue w/Zoom ZCraw or Green Pumpkin Fluke 3. Firecraw w/Speed Craw

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen runs down his three favorite colors for squarebill crankbaits in the fall. Another essential aspect to a squarebill that Lowen cherishes is a circuit board bill vs a plastic bill. It gives the crankbait the feel and characteristic of a balsa crankbait while maintaining the durability of a plastic crankbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes talks about the shallow nature of fish even when the temperatures are dropping across the country. The first feeling anglers have when the water temperatures drop is to fish deeper water but Cifuentes mentions how even in the Ozarks bass will hang out around shallow wood and rock still keyed in on a bigger meal that imitates dying baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Austin Felix
programme.desc: Austin Felix gives his thoughts on when he picks up a Dropshot versus a Ned Rig and a Neko Rig. Speed is often the determining factor for each presentation and he tends to reserve the Neko for largemouth situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brock Mosley
programme.desc: Brock Mosley praises the most versatile lure in bass fishing the Yamamoto Senko. He shows how you can quickly switch from fishing the Senko weightless wacky rigged to adding a weight and changing the hook positioning for a Neko Rig. This lure will get fish to bite every day of the year depending on how you rig it.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cody Huff
programme.desc: Cody Huff explores the benefits he's found when using various spoons during the late summer. He has dialed in his setups and doesn't experiment with multiple brands of spoons but rather uses the same spoons and changes sizes based on situation. From a magnum spoon to a compact jigging spoon Huff has found success on these from the Tennessee River to the Ozarks and many places in between.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Easton Fathergill
programme.desc: Easton Fothergill gives his daily adjustment to how fish were positioned each day of the Classic. From windy days to calm moments Fothergill kept adjusting his tackle to maximize efficiency.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Robert Gee
programme.desc: Robert Gee reflects on his 2024 success with largemouth smallmouth and spotted bass noting that spots and smallmouth chase differently than largemouth requiring presentation adjustments. He shares his preferred head sizes go-to knot and a simple rod and reel setup most anglers can use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Caleb Sumrall
programme.desc: Caleb Sumrall talks about one of the best ways to catch big bass. Sumrall strongly believes in a frog but when bass start shying away or missing it he downsizes instead of changing baits completely. When conditions change bass moods can vary and with that topwater becomes a high risk high reward situation and Sumrall will downsize to the keep the odds in his favor.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Crews
programme.desc: John Crews offers a different option for enticing schooling fish to bite when it gets tough and pressured in the summer. Using a Spy Bait can offer up another look that is great for casting and mimicking baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock explains a new bait he was introduced to that helps him catch not only deep northern smallmouth but also southern largemouth in the winter months. He also discusses the value in 2D sonar with this technique around structure in the south.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Atkins
programme.desc: Justin Atkins sheds light on the flats. A vast area of consistent contour depths and also a place where baitfish and bass congregate as the season turns to cooler temperatures in the fall. This can be a great landing spot for bass as they get positioned to feed during this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Patrick Walters
programme.desc: Elite Series Champion Patrick Walters gives the details of his approach at Lake Murray. Walters relied on a few baits throughout the week to win the event wire to wire. When fish were active and schooling Walters utilized a Zoom Super Fluke and a Rapala Jowler.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey goes through what he would consider his spring selection for largemouth fishing. Spring means March and April in the south but can mean April May and June up north. Downey opts for a crankbait swim jig and two types of soft plastics when making the spring transition.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: Greg Hackney gives some love to an often-forgotten lure for smallmouth fishing and that is the good ole fashioned tube. Hackney still appreciates what a tube brings to the table while fishing for smallmouth on competition days.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyoya Fujita
programme.desc: Kyoya Fujita gives the specifics of his lures that helped him win at Toledo Bend. Fujita was using a technique called "mid-strolling" to get his Jackall Drift Fry and his Deps Sakamata Shad to the correct depth to target suspended bass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kenta Kimura
programme.desc: Kenta Kimura gives some suggestions to be better with the Megabass Magdraft swimbait. He changes the treble to his signature Ryugi quad-hook design for better hookups and he also adds a split ring to the line tie for increased head action and roll. Those two things are essential for Kimura along with finding the right speed on retrieve.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Taku Ito
programme.desc: Taku Ito goes through two key baits to his Bassmaster Elite Series victory at Smith Lake. From Neko Rigging a bluegill imitating bait to dropshotting a Magnum Fuzzy Dice he managed the biggest bass and bag to win.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey dishes out a few of his must-have baits for the early fall fishing season for Smallmouth bass. Downey who lives in Minnesota knows how incredible the bite can be this time of year before cold temps hit daily. Given the type of lake Downey has options for you in this video.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brad Whatley
programme.desc: Brad Whatley gives his strategy of covering water around the spawn when there is thicker cover present. Whatley winds his weighted swimbait around spawning areas and will trigger strikes or boils revealing where bass are positioned to catch on another tactic if necessary.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen goes through two baits he always has rigged up this time of year. A tube and a jig are staples in Lowen's boat and he explains how both get fished in conjunction with one another. There are a few variables like pegging his weight or letting it free flow and also line size in these situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jacob Foutz
programme.desc: Jacob Foutz walks us through his process of selecting sizes of jig heads when targeting bass in flooded timber. His sizes are as follows; 3/16 oz (5 to 10 feet) 1/4 oz (10 to 15 feet) 3/8 oz (20 feet and deeper). Foutz doesn't like getting any heavier than that if he can because of the leverage it gives fish to easily jump and throw the hook.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube discusses his use of a deep diving jerkbait to cover water depths from 4 feet out to 15 feet or so. Dube exclusively uses 10 to 12-pound line and will change his cadence from fast early in the retrieve to slower in the strike zone.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New goes through some of the keys he likes in his jig when targeting bass in the prespawn. New breaks down his jig trailer and why it's efficient and also explains an adjustment to his jig size that he used to never use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock discusses the rising trend of using a swimbait in the prespawn as a substitute for commonly thrown baits with similar profiles. Fished around the same shallow cover it can trigger the big kicker bite tournament anglers seek.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: One of the best structure fishermen in the world Brandon Palaniuk talks about isolated structure in the fall season. BP also gives a few bait suggestions including his handy dropshot.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New lays out one of his favorite topwater presentations the Buzz Toad. Pioneered by his good friend and fellow Elite Todd Auten New likes to use this bait to imitate multiple types of forage bass will eat in the post-spawn.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Roberston
programme.desc: Matt Robertson talks about upsizing his spinnerbait and adjusting his blade sizes when throwing this lure in water temperatures varying from the 40's to 50's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: The Shad Spawn is a unique stage of the fishing season that bridges the gap from the bass spawn into the post spawn. Shad spawning around hard shallow cover gives bass a great opportunity to feed heavily in a short window of time. Not all places in the country feature a shad spawn but if threadfin are present in your lake a shad spawn is likely to happen. Low-light conditions early in the morning are helpful and baits like a spinnerbait imitate small shad perfectly to load the boat for Greg Hackney in a hurry.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Pat Schlapper
programme.desc: Pat Schlapper recounts his finest tournament week to date where to took the title at the Sabine River. Schlapper relied on a few areas of the Sabine along with a few lures including a Do-It Molds compact jig he pours himself altering it with a smaller stouter hook. He also utilized a Brazalo Custom Lures Bushwhacker Buzz Bait in the morning on the final day when it put multiple quality fish in the boat.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Card
programme.desc: Brandon Card gives his thoughts on early season jerkbait fishing. Card gives scenarios when he will opt for a different cadence for his jerkbait rod length and line size.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses the tricky period immediately after bass leave the bed and are either guarding fry or recovering from the spawn. Here is how Christie opts to catch them.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Ed Laughran III
programme.desc: Lake Champlain Champion Ed Loughran runs through his jig setup that accounted for most of the fish throughout his tournament. He also leaned on a topwater in practice and on Championship Monday to catch smallmouth.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Wes Logan
programme.desc: Wes Logan talks moving water and how he approaches it. Being from the Coosa River Logan is used to fishing moving water no matter the time of year and these three baits help him have good success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Florida pro Bernie Schultz talks buzzbaits specifically two kinds. He keeps a squeaking buzzbait and clacking buzzbait ready to go at all times especially in the post-spawn. Although it's an excellent technique in the post-spawn Schultz acknowledges its use early in the year in places like Florida Texas and other southern states. Buzz it slow or fast make it clack or squeak add a toad or a trailer hook whatever you'd like with a buzzbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston gives a quick bait breakdown of a key lure that helped him win the 2024 Bassmaster Elite Series event at the St. Lawrence River. Johnston battled the waves out in Lake Ontario on the final two days of the event to secure a win his second of the season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock explains a new bait he was introduced to that helps him catch not only deep northern smallmouth but also southern largemouth in the winter months. He also discusses the value in 2D sonar with this technique around structure in the south.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Roberston
programme.desc: Matt Robertson talks about upsizing his spinnerbait and adjusting his blade sizes when throwing this lure in water temperatures varying from the 40's to 50's.

programme.desc: Austin Felix gives his thoughts on when he picks up a Dropshot versus a Ned Rig and a Neko Rig. Speed is often the determining factor for each presentation and he tends to reserve the Neko for largemouth situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Seth Feider
programme.desc: Seth Feider goes through his wood jig and grass jig setup. He explains the differences in line tie and weed guard why he likes a short hook and his colors for flipping. Whether it's docks laydowns shoreline grass or submerged vegetation; Feider will often rely on a jig to get it done. His favorite size is a 5/8 ounce.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cliff Prince
programme.desc: Cliff Prince dials us in on his 1/2 ounce Chatterbait setup that helped him win the Bassmaster Elite at Wheeler Lake. He also dishes the details on his magic spot and why he thinks the morning was incredible every day for him.
